findings.problem: Closing.drift opens and hashes root/rel for every .kit-snapshot key starting with .claude/, with no '..' check: an edited snapshot key like .claude/../.env makes close read (never print) a file outside the kit; .kit-snapshot is not in CWK_GUARDED.
SECRET_RE mirrors the kit-wide list, which misses .envrc, .env-local, id_rsa/id_ed25519, *.p12/*.pfx, .netrc, secrets.*, *-credentials.json; the fix belongs to the kit-wide list.
The auto-allowed kit-track.py command runs python3 without -I, unlike the kit hooks (hardening; same shape as the other script allows).

An OSError after git worktree add (copy, sha256, snapshot write) escapes as a traceback and leaves a half-populated worktree and branch, against the docstring's 'a refusal creates and removes nothing'.
Copy-back is not atomic and reports are printed after the loop: a failure at copy N leaves copies 1..N-1 landed with no list of what landed.

The .kit-snapshot manifest is not schema-checked: malformed JSON crashes close; an edited hash value can turn a sidecar into an overwrite or skip an owned copy-back. Validate dict[str, 64-hex] with safe keys and guard the file.
git ls-files targets are pathspecs that may carry glob characters from track filenames (fails safe: over-match only); harden with --literal-pathspecs.
